tools.name: Glob
tools.description:
Find files by glob pattern, sorted by modification time (most recent first).

Powered by ripgrep. Respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` by default — set `include_ignored` to also match ignored files (e.g. build outputs, `node_modules`). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always filtered out. Matches are files only — directories themselves are never listed; to find a directory, glob for a file inside it (e.g. `**/fixtures/**`).

Good patterns:
- `*.ts` — all files matching an extension, at any depth below the search root (a bare pattern without `/` matches recursively)
- `src/*.ts` — files directly inside `src/` (one level, not recursive)
- `src/**/*.ts` — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor and extension
- `**/*.py` — recursive walk from the search root for an extension
- `*.{ts,tsx}` — brace expansion is supported
- `{src,test}/**/*.ts` — cartesian brace expansion is supported too

Results are capped at the first 100 matching paths. If a search would return more, a truncation marker is appended. Refine the pattern (extension, subdirectory) when 100 is not enough, or call again with a narrower anchor.

Large-directory caveat — avoid recursing into dependency / build output even with an anchor, especially when `include_ignored` is set:
- `node_modules/**/*.js`, `.venv/**/*.py`, `__pycache__/**`, `target/**` can produce thousands of results that truncate at the match cap and waste context. Prefer specific subpaths like `node_modules/react/src/**/*.js`.

path.description: Directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Defaults to the current working directory.

include_ignored.description: Also match files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

include_dirs.description: Deprecated and ignored. Results are always files-only — directories are never listed. Accepted only so older calls that still pass this flag are not rejected by parameter validation.

Investigation complete. Here is the full behavioral specification.

## Program structure (`test15_executable`)

- `initialize()` produces no observable output. With no arguments: no output, exit 0.
- For `i = 1 .. min(argc-1, 5)` (i.e. only `argv[1]`–`argv[5]`; extra args ignored), prints one line each:
  1. `pluralize(argv[i])`
  2. `camelize(argv[i])`
  3. `underscore(argv[i])` — only when `i` is even (i=2, 4)
- Then, if `argc > 1`, prints three more lines: `isPlural(argv[1])` (`0`/`1`), `isSingular(argv[1])`, `demodulize("Module::" + argv[1])`.
- Every line is `\n`-terminated (including a trailing empty line when a result is empty). No prompts, no extra whitespace.
- If `demodulize` throws (see below), all prior stdout lines are printed, then libstdc++ terminate message on stderr: `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::out_of_range' / what(): basic_string::substr: __pos (which is N) > this->size() (which is M)`, process dies with SIGABRT, exit code **134**.

## `pluralize(w)` — naive

- `""` → `""`
- If `w` exactly (case-sensitive) equals one of the 10 uncountables `equipment, information, rice, money, species, series, fish, sheep, jeans, police` → `w` unchanged.
- Otherwise → `w + "s"`. No other rules whatsoever: `box→boxs`, `bus→buss`, `church→churchs`, `category→categorys`, `person→persons`, `child→childs`, `mouse→mouses`, `knife→knifes`, `news→newss` (news is NOT uncountable), `Fish→Fishs`, `Jeans→Jeanss`, `" fish"→" fishs"`, `"fish "→"fish s"`, `salmon→salmons`, `_`→`_s`, non-ASCII untouched (`café→cafés`... byte append).

## `camelize(w)` — lower camelCase, underscores only

Byte-wise state machine: skip every `_` byte; the first non-underscore byte after any run of underscores is passed through single-byte `toupper` (C locale; non-ASCII bytes unchanged). Nothing else is changed — the first character is NOT uppercased, and `-`/space/digits are untouched.

- `hello_world→helloWorld`, `active_record→activeRecord`, `dog→dog`, `HelloWorld→HelloWorld`, `HELLO_WORLD→HELLOWORLD`, `x_y_z→xYZ`
- `_hello→Hello`, `_a_b→AB`, `a__b→aB`, `a_→a`, `_→""`, `__→""`, `""→""`
- `hello-world→hello-world`, `a_1→a1`, `héllo_wörld→hélloWörld`, `a_é→aé` (byte `0xC3` unchanged)

## `underscore(w)` — naive camelCase→snake

Byte-wise over original index `i`: if byte is ASCII `A–Z`, append `_` iff `i > 0`, then append the lowercased byte; else append byte unchanged.

- `HelloWorld→hello_world`, `activeRecord→active_record`, `A→a`, `AB→a_b`, `aB→a_b`, `a1B→a1_b`
- NO acronym collapsing: `HELLOWORLD→h_e_l_l_o_w_o_r_d`, `HTMLParser→h_t_m_l_parser`, `ABCDef→a_b_c_def`, `XMLHttpRequest→x_m_l_http_request`
- Existing `_` kept verbatim (can double up): `Foo_Bar→foo__bar`, `_A→__a`, `snake_case_already→snake_case_already`, `ÉmileTest→Émile_test` (non-ASCII bytes untouched), `""→""`

## `demodulize(s)` — buggy substring

Exactly `s.substr(s.rfind(':') + 2)` — note **single-char** `rfind(':')` and `+2`, so it drops the last colon **plus one extra byte**:
- Called here as `demodulize("Module::" + argv[1])`; since the prefix always contains `::`, `rfind` never fails in-program.
- `dog` → `"og"`, `person` → `"erson"`, `a` → `""`, `ab` → `"b"` (i.e. `argv[1].substr(1)` when `argv[1]` has no `:`)
- `X::Y` → `""`, `X::YY` → `"Y"`, `ns::deep::Name` → `"ame"`, `a:b:c` → `""`, `x:y` → `""`
- **Crash (uncaught `std::out_of_range`, SIGABRT, rc 134)** iff the last `:` is the final byte, i.e. `argv[1]` is empty or ends with `:` (`""`, `:`, `::`, `x:` all abort — after the normal preceding output).
- (Out of program reach: with no `:` in `s`, `npos+2` wraps to `1` → `substr(1)`.)

## `isPlural(w)` / `isSingular(w)`

`isSingular(w)` is always exactly `!isPlural(w)` (verified on ~200 probes; printed as `0`/`1`). Everything is **case-sensitive and byte-oriented**. `isPlural(w)` behaves as "a Rails-2.x-style `singularize(w)` would change `w`", which reduces to:

`isPlural(w) = false` if `w` is in the uncountable list (same 10 words, exact lowercase), or `w` matches `/(n)ews$/` (`news`, `xnews` → 0; but `newss` → 1), or `w == "analysis"`, or `w == "crisis"`.

Otherwise `isPlural(w) = true` iff any of:
- `w` ends in lowercase `s` (generic rule: `cats`, `buses`, `classes`, `wishes`, `quizzes`, `matrices`, `vertices`, `indices`, `toes`, `shoes`, `heroes`, `potatoes`, `analyses`, `bases`, `theses`, `syntheses`, `wives`, `knives`, `wolves`, `thieves`, `movies`, `categories`, `babies`, `soliloquies`, `tives`, `hives`, `statuses`, `aliases`, `crises`, `testes`, `gas`, `this`, `is`, `s`, `ss`, `ies`, `bus`, `class`, `status`, `cactus`, `focus`, `thesis`, `basis`, `diagnosis`, `axis`, `alias` → all 1)
- `w` matches `/(octop|vir)i$/` (`octopi`, `viri` → 1; `cacti`, `foci`, `OCTOPI` → 0)
- `w` matches `/^(m|l)ice$/` (`mice`, `lice` → 1; `dice`, `Mice` → 0)
- `w` matches `/([ti])a$/` (`data`, `media`, `criteria`, `ta`, `ia` → 1; `na`, `phenomena`, `DATA` → 0)

Otherwise `false` (`dog`, `box`, `quiz`, `church`, `hero`, `potato`, `child`, `man`, `men`, `women`, `children`, `feet`, `teeth`, `geese`, `people`, `ox`, `oxen`→1 via... no: `oxen`→1 because... `oxen` ends in `n`? — observed `oxen`→**1**; recheck: `oxen` printed `1`. It doesn't fit the compact rules above! Hmm.)

Wait — `oxen` → `1` was observed. It ends in `n`, no rule above matches. That breaks the compact form: there must be an `/^(ox)en$/ → ox` singular rule. So add: `w` matches `/^oxen$/` (anchored; starts with `oxen`: Rails rule is `/^(ox)en/i`) → 1. Similarly recheck other non-s matches observed: `mice`/`lice` (rule), `octopi`/`viri` (rule), `data`/`media`/`criteria` (rule), `oxen` (rule). All other 1-results end in `s`. So the complete extra patterns are: `/^(ox)en/`, `/(octop|vir)i$/`, `/^(m|l)ice$/`, `/([ti])a$/`.
